note: Long-form craft findings and bugs, ranked. Written by Scout; the improver applies recipe, scene and design items, Studio follows script items.

items.title: Add a loan_prepay maths kind (reduce EMI vs reduce tenure, and tenure after a rate rise)
items.detail: renderer/models/maths.py has emi with a fixed months count, so no long video can show 'the loan ends N months earlier' or 'the tenure stretched by N months'. Add kind loan_prepay: inputs amount, rate_pct, months, prepay, prepay_month (and optional new_rate_pct). Values/figures: emi, interest_base, interest_reduce_emi, emi_reduced, months_reduce_tenure (closed form n = -ln(1 - rB/P)/ln(1+r) on the balance B at prepay_month), interest_reduce_tenure, saved_* for both, plus a balance series for the chart. Recompute independently in the number check. Unblocks topics 2026-10-18-prepay-emi-or-tenure and the tenure half of 2026-10-18-repo-hike-your-emi. Done when a checked example script uses it and number-check passes.
items.reason: loan_prepay added (prepay: lower EMI vs shorter loan). The rate-rise tenure stretch is not in it yet; a new item if a video needs it.

items.title: Add a sip_stepup maths kind (SIP raised by X% every year)
items.detail: Feed topic 2026-10-16-sip-stepup (priority high) and 2026-10-18-lifestyle-inflation both need a yearly step-up, which the sip kind cannot express. Add kind sip_stepup: monthly, step_pct, rate_pct, years; values final, invested, gains, final_flat (same start, no step-up) and a yearly series for both, for the chart scene's series/series2. Closed form per year (sum of yearly annuity blocks), recomputed independently in the number check. Done when a checked example script renders the two-line chart in stills.

items.title: End each chapter with a one-line recap card holding its key figure
items.detail: Teacher-style channels (CA Rachana Ranade's long videos) keep viewers through long explanations by closing each section with the one thing to remember. In long_story scripts, make the last beat of each chapter a bignumber with a kicker line 'So far' and the chapter's one computed figure, 3-4 s, before the next chapter card. A/B via a script flag so improvement.evaluate can compare average % viewed at chapter boundaries. Works if retention dips at chapter cards shrink in the experiment arm.

items.title: Open long videos on a concrete moment the viewer has lived (an SMS, a payslip, an app button)
items.detail: The channels that win long-form here (Labour Law Advisor's mis-selling and EPF videos, this week's repo/EMI videos) open on the viewer's own situation, not on a concept. In the first beat of every long_story script, put a cast member in one recognisable moment (bank SMS 'rate revised', appraisal letter, the prepay button in the app) with the rupee stake as a computed figure on screen within 5 s; the concept explanation comes after the first chapter card. Studio applies it when writing; check it in the Saturday review of the first 30 s.

items.title: New scene: an 'inputs' form that fills itself in before a calculation
items.detail: Calculator-led channels (Asset Yogi's spreadsheet walk-throughs) earn trust by showing the inputs before the answer. We have no scene for that: add an inputs scene to remotion/src/scenes showing 3-4 labelled fields (amount, rate, years, step-up) typing in one by one from the beat's maths figures, with an 'assumption' tag on the rate, then handing off to split/chart. All values come from the timeline figures, never typed. Behind a flag; look at it in stills first. Works if it passes the layout probe and liveliness, and % viewed holds through the setup beats in the experiment arm.

items.title: Feed topics named a removed template (long_explainer)
items.detail: The four 2026-10-16 topics listed templates ['long_explainer'], which was removed with the Pillow engine; the only long template is long_story. Fixed today in improvement/longform/topics.json (Scout's file). If generator.run state matches topics by template, check it ignores unknown names rather than silently dropping topics. No action needed unless that check fails.

items.title: check-plan demands #Shorts on long videos
items.detail: generator/run.py check_plan fails every plan without #Shorts, including format long (L-20261018-01). A landscape 4-minute video should not carry #Shorts. Studio shipped without it (ship does not need the planner step). Fix: apply the rule only when plan_format(plan) == 'short', and add a test.
items.reason: Already fixed: check_plan applies the #Shorts rule only when the plan format is short.

items.title: reveal/bignumber centre text runs under an actor at x 0.86
items.detail: QA on L-20261018-01 (beat future-self, ~127 s): the hero line 'paid by future Rohan' ran under Rohan, hiding the last word; the layout probe did not flag it. Fix in the scene: limit the text column to the area clear of the actor, or let the probe treat actors as obstacles. Studio worked around it by dropping the actor.

items.title: A stage opening needs its stake on screen from frame one
items.detail: QA failed L-20261018-01's first render: a stage beat (Rohan reading the bank SMS) showed no text until 3.5 s. Fixed with a chip at 'start' carrying the computed interest jump. Script rule for Studio: when the first beat is a stage moment, its chip (or a reveal line) shows a computed figure at 'start'. QA still calls a chip weaker than a big number; a bigger hook card over a stage scene would be a scene item.

items.title: Say the video's promise in one line between 20 and 30 seconds
items.detail: Retention guides agree on three beats for the first 30 s: prove the title with one concrete example (0-10 s), say why it matters to the viewer (10-20 s), then a one-line roadmap of what they will know by the end (20-30 s), repeating the title's number if it has one. Our first long video (L-20261018-01) does the first two well (bank SMS, then the interest stake in beat 2) but beat 4 ends on 'Let's find out why', which promises nothing specific. Studio: make the 3rd-4th beat a promise line naming two or three things the viewer will know (e.g. 'how long, how much, and the one number on your statement that fixes it'). No greeting, no channel intro, no full table of contents. How we know: first-30-second retention in YouTube Studio once long videos have views; until then, check every long script has such a line before 30 s.

items.title: End each chapter with a one-line tease of the next one (open loop)
items.detail: Explainer retention advice: open a loop every 2-3 minutes by teasing the next part before it starts ('and that was the good year'), and close the main question only in the last fifth. Build it as a flag `long_chapter_tease`: in the variant, Studio writes a tease line as the last beat before each `chapter` beat, and the chapter card shows it as its subtitle for the first second. Control: chapters as now. Pairs with, but is separate from, the 2026-10-18 recap-card experiment (recap looks back, tease looks forward); don't run both in the same video. Decide on % viewed per long video with improvement.evaluate.

items.title: Put the biggest reveal about two thirds of the way in, not at the end
items.detail: Saving the best figure for the finale loses the viewers who leave before it; guides put the best moment at about two thirds of the runtime and keep the end for the 'what to do' and recap. Studio: when ordering chapters, place the side-by-side or gap reveal (the video's biggest computed number) at 60-70% of the planned length. The four new 2026-10-19 topic outlines already mark where it goes. How we know: the reveal beat's start / duration_sec in render.json lands between 0.6 and 0.7.

items.title: card_min_due's docstring tells the writer the video mentions GST, wrong for US/UK cards
items.detail: renderer/models/maths.py card_min_due says real cards 'add GST on interest and fees ... The video says so'. GST is Indian; since the channel went global (2026-10-18) a USD card story must not say GST. Improver: change the docstring to 'taxes or fees on interest where they apply (GST in India)' and, if long_story/README.md or short_story/README.md repeat the GST line for card stories, make it country-aware. How we know: no non-INR script mentions GST.

items.title: A stage chip set 'at: start' is not visible on frame 0
items.detail: QA failed L-20261019-01's first render: the opening stage beat's chip ('Minimum due: $150', at: start) animates in after frame 0, so the first frame showed only Rohan in a room. bignumber/reveal lines at start are already drawn on frame 0 (data.tsx Lines: p.beat.from === 0 && start < 0.05). Improver: give the stage Chip the same frame-0 rule. Until then Studio opens on a bignumber with plain-text start lines (no value, which counts up from zero) and the actor beside them. This supersedes the 2026-10-18-first-frame-hook workaround.

items.title: camera push on a screen beat zooms its title out of the frame
items.detail: L-20261019-01's first render failed the layout gate ('Minimum only' outside the frame at 109 s): the screen scene's title sits at the top of the wall screen and the push camera scales the frame 1.09x. Fixed by using drift. Improver: keep screen content inside the push-safe area, or have the camera clamp scale for scenes with a top caption. Script rule for Studio meanwhile: no push on screen beats with a title.

items.title: A trailer Short can be blocked by the Shorts category window
items.detail: The trailer for L-20261019-01 (credit_card) failed check-plan twice: credit_card was used by v-20261019-02 within the last 3 Shorts. A trailer must keep the long video's topic, so it cannot be relabelled; it was marked failed (v-20261019-04). Options: Scout prefers long topics whose category is not in the last 3 Shorts on Studio days, or the owner decides whether trailers are exempt from the category window (variety.py is owner-only). A later Studio run can still make this trailer once credit_card leaves the window, if the one-trailer-per-long-video rule allows it.

items.title: prop stack: kicker and figure share one spot; without a kicker the figure leaves the frame
items.detail: L-20261019-01 (second try, failed): beat 'total' used prop 'stack' with kicker 'Minimum only, all in' and text '{card_total_paid}' (value counting up). QA saw the kicker and the figure drawn on top of each other for the whole beat. With the kicker removed, the layout gate failed: '$11,638' at 131.7 s outside the frame (camera punch:cost). Improver: lay out stack's kicker above the figure and keep the figure inside the push/punch-safe area. Until then Studio avoids the stack prop for a headline figure (use cheque, receipt, vault or tag, which rendered cleanly).

items.title: road signs overflow with long labels; a second sign runs off the right edge
items.detail: L-20261019-01 beat 'recap' (road, two signs 'Minimum only' / 'Fixed payment' with figures): QA saw the label spill over the board and the second board cut off ('Fixed payme'). The board is a fixed 340 px scaled up to 2.1x as it approaches. Improver: size the board to its text and clamp it inside the frame. Studio rule meanwhile: road sign labels of at most ~10 characters ('Year one', 'Still paying' rendered fine).

items.title: Script rule: never set presenter.x to 0
items.detail: Thirteen presenters with x: 0 were centred on the left edge, cutting the actor in half (QA, L-20261019-01). Leave x out: the long-video default (0.84) keeps them on the right. Optionally the improver can make the probe or the build reject x < 0.1 for presenters.

items.title: Script rule: a prop's text is a figure, not a phrase
items.detail: prop 'receipt' with text 'Pay off in three years' ran outside the frame (layout gate, L-20261019-01 render 1). Put a placeholder figure in text and the words in kicker/sub.

items.title: number check flags chapter timestamps in a long video's description
items.detail: generator/numbers.py check_claims treats '0:00 Intro', '1:14 ...' as unbacked numbers, so a description with the chapter list (which studio.md requires) fails number-check. Studio works around it by running number-check before adding the timestamps, which leaves the shipped description unchecked. Fix: skip lines matching ^\d+:\d\d\s in the description (only for format long), with a test.

items.title: Card minimum-payment remake is written and fact-checked: retry the render
items.detail: videos/L-20261019-01/script.json (58 beats, ~1,025 words, 4:37, new bill/road/fork/source scenes, fact review passed) failed only on layout after two re-renders. A later Studio run can reuse it with the 'total' beat moved off the stack prop (e.g. prop cheque or vault) under a new id; the topic 2026-10-19-card-minimum-trap stays usable. Done 2026-10-19: rendered as L-20261019-02 (qa_passed, 277 s, liveliness median 1.95).

items.title: Answer the title's question no earlier than ~75%, and keep one loop open after it
items.detail: In L-20261019-02 the main question (minimum vs fixed payment, 'two roads') is fully answered at 72-76% (beats 'fork'/'split', ~200-212 s of 277), then 24% of the runtime is a source card, a checklist and a recap. Per YouTube's key-moments help, the audience shrinks as a video goes on; creator guides consistently name 'a pivot that feels like an ending' as the main mid/late dip cause. Rule for long_story scripts: (1) the side-by-side resolution sits at 75-85%; (2) before it, name one thing still to come ('and the fix is already printed on your statement') so the action steps are a payoff, not an epilogue; (3) the recap beat is at most one beat and 10 s. Add to the long_story README recipe checklist. Worked when: the share of runtime after the resolution beat is <= 20% in render.json, and once the curve exists, hold at 90% vs hold at 70%.

items.title: A re-hook line at every chapter start, not just a chapter card
items.detail: Chapter cards in L-20261019-02 sit at 11%, 29%, 39%, 62%, 84%, 93%. A chapter card with no spoken line is a silent pause, the kind of slow stretch creator guides identify as the dip point (one worked example: a 45 s stretch without narration lost 35% of viewers). The first beat after each chapter card should restate the stake in one sentence with a figure (e.g. 'Twelve months in, and he still owes {card_owed_year1}'), and the gap between two such re-hooks should be <= 90 s. This differs from the chapter-tease experiment (a line at the end of the chapter before): this one is the opening line of the next. Add to the long_story README. Worked when: no stretch longer than 90 s between beats that carry a placeholder figure (checkable in timeline.json).

items.title: Export hold at each chapter start for long videos
items.detail: workers/stats.ts already stores each upload's retention curve (Upload.retention) and computes hookHold from it. For long videos, also compute the hold at each chapter start (render.json 'chapters' has the times; workers/lib/retention.ts holdAt interpolates) and write it to metrics/videos.json as 'chapterHolds': [{t, hold}]. Then Scout's Saturday review and improvement.evaluate can see which chapter loses viewers instead of guessing. YouTube only shows key moments for videos >= 60 s with >= 100 views, so this stays empty until the long videos get views. Lane: the auditor (workers/) or improver; no new YouTube scope needed, the curve is already fetched. Worked when: metrics/videos.json carries chapterHolds for every long video with a curve.

items.title: Give the rule-of-the-video beat a second picture so a rewatch spike means value, not confusion
items.detail: YouTube notes a spike (rewatch) can mean a segment was valuable or unclear. Our densest explanations (L-20261019-02 'statement'/'minimum is worked out' beats, ~45-60 s) say a percentage and a floor in one breath over one picture. When a beat explains how a figure is computed, split it into two beats: the rule in words, then the rule applied to the story's own number with a placeholder. Script rule for the long_story README. Worked when: no beat in the 'how it works' chapter carries more than one new placeholder.

items.title: chart/screen: shade the gap between the two lines and label it with its figure
items.detail: Rich vs poor, early vs late and every 'same money, two paths' chapter is a story about the gap, but our charts draw two glowing lines and leave the viewer to see the distance. Add optional `gap` {text: '{name.key}', at} to `chart` and `screen` (remotion/src/scenes/data.tsx ChartScene, and the screen scene): fill the area between `series` and `series2` up to the drawing head in the good colour at ~25% opacity, and at `gap.at` pop a chip at the right end, midway between the two lines, holding the figure. The figure must be a placeholder from maths (a difference of two results needs the `compare` kind below, or an existing `gains` key). Behind an A/B flag `chart-gap-fill`. Worked when: stills of the 2026-10-21-same-salary-rich-vs-poor chapters show the chip inside the plot, clear of both lines, layout gate passes; then evaluate on % viewed of the chart beats.

items.title: New maths kind `compare`: the difference and ratio of two named results
items.detail: Rich vs poor and early vs late videos need 'the gap' as one figure (₹1.50 Cr vs ₹34.9 L is a ₹1.15 Cr gap). Today the writer can only show both numbers. Add `compare` to renderer/models/maths.py: inputs `a` and `b` ('name.value_key', both computed earlier in the same maths list), figures `diff` (a-b, fm.short), `ratio` (times(a/b)), `pct` (how much bigger in %). Mirror it in the number check's closed-form recompute and add tests (tests only grow). Worked when: number-check passes a script using {gap.diff} and rejects a hard-coded gap.

items.title: New maths kind `fee_take`: a fee as a share of an amount, over a year and over N years
items.detail: Both how_they_make_money topics added today (credit cards, banks) need 'the shop pays 2% of every swipe: on ₹30,000 a month that is ₹7,200 a year'. Add `fee_take` to renderer/models/maths.py: inputs `amount` (per period), `fee_pct`, `per_year` (12 for monthly), `years`; figures `per_period`, `per_year_total`, `total`, `fee_pct`; series: the cumulative take by year (so it can be a chart). Number check and tests as for every kind. Worked when: Studio can write the swipe-fee chapter with only placeholders.

items.title: chart: a live value label riding the leading dot
items.detail: Every top animated money channel counts the number up at the tip of the line as it draws (the 'counter' and 'wipe' techniques together, onlinejournalismblog 2026-06-23). Ours draws a pulsing dot with no number, and the figure only appears in a chip or a later beat. In ChartScene add optional `tip1`/`tip2` = a figure placeholder: a chip beside the head dot that counts up with `counted()` from 0 to the series' final value, landing on the Python-formatted string exactly when drawTo is reached (count-ups only fill the frames before it lands, as data.tsx already does). Flag `chart-tip-counter`. Worked when: the last still of a chart beat shows the formatted final figure at the line's end, inside the frame and the right-edge zone.

items.title: chart: the line the story is not about goes neutral grey
items.detail: Video chart guidance: one strong colour for the focus, everything else grey or pale, so the eye knows where to look. Our charts draw red and green at full glow every time, so the viewer has two focal points. Add optional `focus: 1|2` to chart/screen: the other series draws in pal.muted at 60% opacity with no drop-shadow. Script rule for Studio once flagged: set focus on the line the sentence is about. Flag `chart-focus`; evaluate on % viewed.

items.title: chart: start zoomed on the first years, then zoom out to the whole curve
items.detail: The classic compounding reveal: the first 5 years look flat and boring, then the axis rescales and the curve shoots up. It is a built-in 'wait for it' at the moment viewers drift. Add optional `zoomAt` (event) to ChartScene: until zoomAt the y and x scales fit the series up to the head; from zoomAt they ease (0.8 s) to the full ticks. Tick labels re-fade at the new scale. Flag `chart-zoom-out`; best used in the level 5 chapter of 2026-10-21-money-levels-india. Worked when: two stills either side of zoomAt show different scales and both pass the layout gate.

items.title: Script rule: a chart's spoken line states the takeaway, and a chart holds at most two lines
items.detail: Studio rule for long_story (renderer/templates/long_story/README.md, 'chart' and 'screen'): the beat's `say` and the screen's `title` state the conclusion ('Starting ten years late costs more than a crore'), not the subject ('Here is the chart'). L-20261019-02 opened its chart beats with 'Here is the whole journey' and 'Look how the red line...'. Build in stages: drawFrom/drawTo and marks tied to events in the spoken line, one new figure per beat. Never more than two series; anything else is a `split` or `prop`.

items.title: Reset feed topics had empty demand URLs
items.detail: The three topics added with the 2026-10-21 reset had `demand.url` "". I filled the middle-class one (Dhruv Rathee, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D7Y-nJ8uiEA, 10.06M). The other two reference videos are listed in formats.json without URLs too; Studio can cite the reference by title. Research could fill URLs in formats.json examples on its next run.

items.title: renderer/remotion.py keeps old stills and probe frames between renders
items.detail: render_timeline does not clear /tmp/remotion-<id>/stills and probe before rendering. After L-20261021-01 got 30 s longer, preview.png still showed an end card at 471.5 s from the earlier render, and the probe kept 19 stale frames. That could pass or fail QA on frames the video no longer has. Fix: empty both folders at the start of a render. How we know: after a re-render, every file in stills/ has the new mtime.

items.title: render.json reports tempo 1.0 for long videos rendered at 1.5
items.detail: L-20261021-01: timeline.json has tempo and speed 1.5, but render.json says tempo 1.0 (L-20261019-02 too). The dashboard or the evaluator may read the wrong pace. Fix: write the timeline's tempo into render.json.

items.title: Money props show ₹0 until their `at` event when they have a `value`
items.detail: A tag, cheque or stack prop with `value` and a late `at` showed '₹0' for up to 6.5 s (L-20261021-01 l1-trap, l4-sip, l4-gains; QA round 1), then counted up after the voice had already said the figure. Studio worked around it by dropping `value` and using at: start. Scene fix: hide the figure, not show 0, before `at`, or start the count at `start`. Script rule meanwhile: a prop's `at` is the word just before the figure is spoken, or `start`.

items.title: The vault prop's door covers the left of its figure
items.detail: QA, L-20261021-01: the vault hid the ₹ of ₹2,40,000, all but ',816' of ₹18,211, and all but 'L' of ₹64.0 L. Studio swapped in piggy, bucket and stack. Scene fix: put the figure clear of the door, or on a plaque above it.

items.title: The receipt prop draws its total in the caption band
items.detail: QA, L-20261021-01 l3-total (round 2): the receipt's '₹1.4 L' sat at the bottom of the frame under the word-by-word captions for the whole beat, with or without a kicker. Studio used the tag prop instead. Scene fix: keep the receipt total above about 75% of the frame height.

items.title: The snowball scene's tick labels are pale pink on white snow
items.detail: QA, L-20261021-01: '+ returns' ticks were nearly unreadable, and one sat at the top-left edge, next to the Sikka mark. Studio replaced the beat with a stack prop. Scene fix: a dark chip behind tick text and a safe-area clamp.

items.title: Calendar sub-label loses word spacing
items.detail: QA, L-20261021-01 l4-cal: 'Same date, same amount' rendered as 'Same date, sameamount'. Probably a line-wrap or kerning bug in the calendar sub text.

items.title: Script rule: a long chapter title is at most about 20 characters
items.detail: The probe failed 'Money works harder than you' (27 characters) on the chapter card as running outside the frame, while 'Your money gets a job' (21) passed. Keep chapter titles to about 20 characters, or have the improver let the card wrap to two lines.

items.title: Script rule: one checklist beat per highlighted item
items.detail: Checklist `active` is fixed for the whole beat. A beat that speaks two items leaves the highlight on the first while the voice is on the second (QA, L-20261021-01 which-1 and which-3). Split such lines into one beat per item. A scene option to move `active` on an event would allow longer beats.

items.title: No maths kind for a year of living costs in the future
items.detail: To compare a pot's yearly growth with future yearly spending, Studio fed a yearly amount into price_rise's `monthly` input (L-20261021-01 'life'); only {life_new_monthly} is valid there. The fact reviewer twice failed level six for comparing like with unlike (year-20 growth vs today's spending; then a pot that couldn't also keep up with inflation). A `living_cost` or `withdrawal` kind (yearly cost after N years, and the pot whose real growth covers it) would make level-of-wealth stories safe to write.

items.title: A long video's mp4 can't leave a cloud session: 244 MB is over GitHub's 100 MB push limit, and Releases are refused
items.detail: L-20261021-01 (8:22, about 4 Mbps) shipped its manifest to main, but `ship --release` got HTTP 403 (cloud sessions may not create releases) and `--media-branch` was rejected (GH001: file over 100 MB). Every long video will be over 100 MB at this bitrate. Options for the improver or owner: encode long videos so the mp4 stays under about 95 MB (about 1.5 Mbps at 8 min), or split the mp4 into parts on media/<id> for release-video.yml to rejoin, or use Git LFS. Until then the owner uploads it locally.
items.resolution: Fixed 2026-10-21: media branches carry a long mp4 in 90 MB parts that release-video.yml joins; Studio ships with --media-branch, not --release.

items.title: Test & Compare thumbnails are three copies of one picture
items.detail: All three thumbnails of L-20261021-01 (and of L-20261019-01/-02) use layout 'story' with the same hero (piggy or card), the same receipt, arrow, background and character spot; only the words and figures change. YouTube's own Test & Compare help says variants must be 'meaningfully different' or the test runs long and ends inconclusive, and it picks the winner by watch-time share. Change: the long_story README's `thumbnails` row requires the three thumbnails to use three different layouts (story, versus, secret) or at least a different hero and cast member; check-plan or the writer prompt rejects two thumbnails with the same layout+hero. Worked when: thumbWinner in metrics/videos.json is set (not inconclusive) for most long videos after 14 days.

items.title: The versus and secret thumbnail layouts exist but no README tells the writer
items.detail: remotion/src/compositions/Thumbnail.tsx renders layout 'versus' (VersusThumb) and 'secret' (SecretThumb) from ThumbFormats.tsx, but renderer/templates/long_story/README.md (line 32-33) only documents layout 'story', so every long video since 2026-10-19 uses story x3. Change: document both layouts and their fields in the long_story README (and short_story if missing), with which angle each suits (versus for rich_vs_poor, secret for how_they_make_money/once_you_understand). Worked when: the next long videos use at least two layouts across their three thumbnails.

items.title: Thumbnail words repeat the title instead of adding to it
items.detail: L-20261021-01: title 'The 6 levels of money in India: which one are you?', thumbnail-b words 'Which money level?'. Thumbnail guides agree the picture should open the curiosity gap and the title give context, never repeat it. Script rule for the long_story README: thumbnail `words` share no content word with the title (stop words aside) and add a feeling or a stake ('Stuck on level 2?', 'Banks love level 2'). Can be a check in check-plan later.

items.title: Write three titles per long video for Test & Compare, not one
items.detail: Test & Compare now tests titles too (title only, thumbnail only, or both; up to 3), winner by watch-time share. We write one title per video. Change: long_story script gets `titles` (two alternates, each a different promise shape: 'The ___ trap, explained' / 'Once you understand ___' / a 'which one are you' question), shown on the dashboard's video page next to the thumbnails so the owner pastes them into Test & Compare when uploading. Needs the manifest and dashboard to carry the field. Worked when: the owner runs title tests and metrics record a winner.

items.title: Long titles: a named thing plus a loaded noun, under ~55 characters, no figures
items.detail: The outliers found today: 'The 'Buy Now Pay Later' Trap, Explained' (39 chars, 6.0M), 'The 'Car Loan' Trap, Explained' (1.2M), 'How the rich avoid paying taxes' (31, 3.9M), 'Every Level Of Wealth In 13 Minutes' (35, 2.5M), 'Why It's More Expensive To Be Poor' (34, 2.6M). Ours: 'Only paying the minimum on a $5,000 card? Here is the real cost' (63), 'Repo rate hiked: the quiet way your home loan gets longer' (57, a news headline). Rule for the long_story README: titles of at most ~55 characters, the subject named first, one loaded word (trap, rich, poor, explained, secretly), figures go on the thumbnail, not the title. Worked when: long-video CTR in metrics rises above the channel's Shorts-free baseline (needs impressions data).

items.title: Add a long `trap_alert` format: 'The ___ trap, explained' (single-trap deep dive)
items.detail: formats.json has trap_alert only for Shorts. The single-trap long shape is proven: 'The Buy Now Pay Later Trap, Explained' 6.04M (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KkN6I3gZfGI), 'The Buy Now Pay Later Trap Is Getting Worse' 2.72M, 'The Car Loan Trap, Explained' 1.23M, 'Stupid & Evil Business Model - Buy Now Pay Later' 1.06M. One trap, 8-12 min: how it hooks you, the maths of it, who profits, how people get out. Scout cannot write formats.json; research or the improver adds a `format: long` entry with id trap_alert (the story id already exists in generator/variety.py), then Scout feeds topics in it (car loan, BNPL, lifestyle EMIs).

items.title: The cast member sits under YouTube's duration badge
items.detail: In the story layout the character fills the bottom-right corner, where YouTube draws the duration badge on long videos (it hides hands and lanyard, not the face, today). Guides say keep critical elements clear of that corner. Check when a new layout is added: no figure or face in the bottom-right ~180x70 px of 1280x720.

items.title: Stop within 30 seconds of the payoff: no checklist re-run of every item at the end
items.detail: L-20261021-01 delivered its payoff (level six) by 7:24 and then spent 58 s (12% of 502 s) restating all six levels as a checklist before the end card. Retention guides agree that 'before the final payoff, the ending runs long' is a main drop point, and that once the payoff lands you shouldn't drift (overseeros, outlierkit: payoff, then one CTA in the last 20-30 s). The rule goes in renderer/templates/long_story/README.md under Shape: after the strongest item's payoff, at most 30 s and about 4 beats (one synthesis line naming the single move, one character beat, the end card with one CTA). The per-item recap belongs in the recap-and-tease beats during the video, not at the end. We'll know it worked when time after the last chapter's payoff is ≤ 6% of runtime in render.json, and when average % viewed on the next long videos holds or rises (improvement.evaluate, long format).

items.title: First recap-and-tease by 2:30, then every 2-3 minutes (the last video's first one came at 4:15)
items.detail: The README asks for a recap-and-tease every 2-3 minutes, but L-20261021-01's first ('So that is three floors') came at 4:15 and its second at 6:20, after three chapters of 64-94 s. Guides put the first big retention dip at about 3:00 and a re-hook just before it. Script rule for long_story: put a recap-and-tease line as the last beat of the chapter that ends nearest 2:30, 5:00 and 7:30 (story seconds at tempo 1.5 ≈ the chapter boundaries after items 2, 4 and 6), each naming what was covered and teasing one concrete thing still to come. To check it, list the recap beats' start times in render.json; the hold at each chapter start (2026-10-20-chapter-hold-metric) will show whether it helps.

items.title: Give the strongest item the most time (it got the least)
items.detail: In L-20261021-01 the chapters ran 64, 73, 94, 64, 63, 60 and 57 s. The card-minimum chapter (item 3, a topic we'd already made a whole video of) was the longest, and the last two items (the payoff) were the shortest. Experiment on the long format: the strongest item's chapter runs 1.5× the average chapter, with two reveals inside it (a figure, then a turn), and no other chapter runs over 1.2× the average. Arm A keeps the current behaviour. Metric: average % viewed and the hold at that chapter's start. Writer instruction text goes through config/experiments.json like the Shorts hook experiment.

items.title: Money formats a negative amount as '$-19,470' / '₹-19,470'
items.detail: maths lumpsum with a negative rate_pct (a car losing 15% a year, which tomorrow's debt topic uses) gives figures.gains = '$-19,470'. The sign belongs before the currency: '−$19,470' (or '-$19,470'), and the same for INR and the short forms. Fix it in renderer/engine/formatting.py Money (full and short) and the mirror in remotion/src/fmt/inr.ts, and add a test for a negative amount in each currency. Also note in the long_story README's maths table that lumpsum accepts a negative rate_pct for something losing value. Until then, writers should show `final`, not `gains`, for a falling value. Check: compute([{kind:'lumpsum', amount:35000, rate_pct:-15, years:5}], Money('USD'))['…']['figures']['gains'] starts with the sign.

items.title: Point every long video's end screen at one specific long video
items.detail: The guides give one CTA, pointing to one specific next video, as the best ending for session watch time. End screens are set in YouTube Studio when uploading, which only the owner does. When there are 2+ long videos, pick the closest one in subject (e.g. the money-levels video for any which_one_are_you or rich_vs_poor video) as the single end-screen element. The spoken CTA on the end card stays a single ask.

items.title: Long shots: a close or medium camera on a stack or phone pushes its tag off the frame
items.detail: First long video on the shot system (L-20261023-01): close shots on a stack (tag sits above the stack top) and close or moving shots in a beat with a phone made the layout probe fail 30+ texts as 'runs outside the frame'. Studio worked around it: phone beats use one medium key on the phone, stack beats stay wide, close-ups only on actor-only beats. Fix in remotion/src/studio/shot.tsx: frame a stack on its tag (not the top + 80 px), and keep every money tag inside the frame when the camera targets an object.

items.title: Long shots: phone text is below 30 px in a wide shot
items.detail: PhoneApp is drawn 280 px wide in 16:9 (380 in a Short), so its lines are ~28 px at camera scale 1 and fail the 30 px minimum; labels over ~9 characters also run into their value ('Market, assumed' / '8%'). Make the long phone wider (~360 px) and let labels wrap or truncate.

items.title: Long shots: the drop-in `word` starts above the frame
items.detail: The shot `word` sits at top h*0.1 (108 px) and drops in from translateY(-260 px), so the probe fails it as off-frame when sampled during the drop (7 words in L-20261023-01). Studio dropped all `word`s from the video. Fix: start the drop from inside the frame on the long format (or shorter drop).

items.title: Long shots: flying notes' sign glyph is 20 px
items.detail: MoneyFlow notes are 100 px wide in 16:9, so the '$' on each note measures ~20-23 px and fails the probe in wide shots (and runs off-frame in close ones). Studio removed all flows. Fix: mark the note glyph data-probe="skip" (decoration) or draw it as a path.

items.title: Script rule: in a phone beat the actor stands near the phone, not on the far spot
items.detail: A medium shot framed on a phone at the right spot crops an actor at the left spot in half (QA, 5 beats). Put the actor at 0.45 (phone right) or 0.55 (phone left).
